StackType.rationale: PowerStackType.Counter. The sim has no StackType concept; Power.on_stack (powers.py:64-66) adds unconditionally, which is what PowerCmd.ModifyAmount does (PowerCmd.cs:236 -- no StackType branch). Third-file citations, not hashed here.

ShouldScaleInMultiplayer.rationale: PlatingPower.cs:23 returns true, feeding PowerCmd.Apply's MultiplayerScalingModel leg (PowerCmd.cs:128-131), already waived as step 14 of audit/records/seam/power_cmd.json. The sim is single-player.

GetScaledAmountForMultiplayer.rationale: PlatingPower.cs:85-88 is ((Players.Count - 1) * 2 + 1) * amount, which is exactly `amount` at one player. Multiplayer-only; same waiver as above.

AfterApplied.rationale: PlatingPower.cs:29-36 sets the Decrement DynamicVar to RunState.Players.Count when the owner is an enemy -- i.e. an enemy's Plating decays once per player per round. At one player that is 1, which is what the sim's _tick (powers.py:1066) does. Multiplayer-only; the CanonicalVars default is 1m (PlatingPower.cs:27) and the sim matches it.

BeforeSideTurnStart.rationale: CLOSED 2026-07-28 (round 3) by the gap-queue continuation's post-section-A pass -- the turn-start split, the combat-over hook gate, Glass Eye's reward set, the out-of-combat potion action and the choose-a-card selector arm. This is a CODE change, not a re-reading of the old code. PlatingPower's round-1 arm now lives on the real hook. `before_side_turn_start` is `Hook.BeforeSideTurnStart` (CombatManager.cs:458) -- fired at the top of PlayerCombatState.start_turn, after the per-turn card-cost reset and before the block clear -- and PlatingPower.cs:41-56's guards are reproduced there (owner not a player, RoundNumber <= 1). The sim's `on_combat_start` implementation is gone, so a combat-start listener that reads an enemy's block now sees it bare, as the game shows it. EXECUTED: test/test_turn_start_split.py::test_plating_grants_its_round_one_block_at_the_turn_start_not_combat_start.  The gap it replaced read: SLOT. C# uses the ROUND-1 arm of a turn-start hook as a stand-in for combat start -- PlatingPower.cs:41-56 fires only when side == Player, the owner is NOT a player, and combatState.RoundNumber <= 1, and its own comment says 'We want enemies that start with Plating to also start combat with block'. Dispatched at CombatManager.cs:458, i.e. AFTER Creature.BeforeTurnStart (:453) and BEFORE the block clear at :496. The sim instead uses the real combat-start hook, on_combat_start (combat.py:208, immediately before start_turn at :209). DORMANT: the two points are adjacent, the enemy's block is not cleared at the player's turn start on either side, and the round-1-only condition is enforced on both (C# by RoundNumber, the sim by on_combat_start firing once). What differs is the sim grants the block one dispatch EARLIER, so any on_combat_start listener registered after this power sees the enemy already blocked where the game shows it unblocked. Named trigger: a combat-start relic or power that reads an enemy's block -- none is ported. Reachable owners are plentiful (monsters/underdocks/sewer_clam.py:30, monsters/underdocks/lagavulin_matriarch.py:43, monsters/hive/slumbering_beetle.py:41, monsters/hive/flail_knight.py:87, monsters/glory/frog_knight.py:42).

BeforeSideTurnEndEarly.issue: CLOSED. PlatingPower moved onto the `_early` pass on BOTH sides: `on_player_turn_end_early` and `before_enemy_side_end_early`, matching PlatingPower.cs:61 and the reason its own comment gives ('so that it triggers before end-of-turn damage effects'). Two orderings become guaranteed rather than lucky: AsleepPower's `_very_early` Plating-drop now always precedes this grant, and Fake Orichalcum's `_very_early` `Block > 0` snapshot always precedes it too, which is the ordering FakeOrichalcum.cs:40-45 spells out in prose. EXECUTED: test_fake_merchant.py::test_fake_orichalcum_is_suppressed_by_platings_earlier_grant and test_enemy_side_per_side.py::TestSideEndListeners.  FIXED 2026-07-28 (round 4). The text it replaced read: NARROWED 2026-07-27. THE SIM NOW HAS PHASE PASSES -- `_PHASES` = very_early/early/plain/late (hooks.py:36), resolved per dispatch by `_each`, and relics really use them (relics/orichalcum.py:30 `on_player_turn_end_very_early`, relics/paels_eye.py:61 `on_player_turn_end_early`). PlatingPower did NOT move: powers.py:1138 is still the plain `on_player_turn_end`, where PlatingPower.cs:58-60 is BeforeSideTurnEndEarly and says why in as many words ('so that it triggers before end-of-turn damage effects'). The executed Constrict witness this entry carried is GONE -- ConstrictPower moved to `after_player_turn_end` (powers.py:1531), strictly after the whole BeforeTurnEnd pass -- so what remains is the phase itself, and any plain-pass turn-end damage effect still races this block on registration order. Both halves verified against today's code.

AfterSideTurnStart.rationale: CLOSED 2026-07-28 (round 3) by the gap-queue continuation's post-section-A pass -- the turn-start split, the combat-over hook gate, Glass Eye's reward set, the out-of-combat potion action and the choose-a-card selector arm. This is a CODE change, not a re-reading of the old code. The player leg is on the real hook: PlatingPower.cs:70's AfterSideTurnStart maps to the new `after_side_turn_start` dispatcher (CombatManager.cs:522, post-draw), and `participants.Contains(Owner)` is what the surviving `player is self.owner` test reproduces. The ENEMY leg is unchanged and stays where this entry always put it -- turn_structure's G5, which owns the per-enemy-vs-per-side mechanism.  The gap it replaced read: WRONG SLOT on the player leg. C#'s AfterSideTurnStart is CombatManager.cs:522, POST-draw; the sim's on_player_turn_start is player.py:169, PRE-draw (before modify_hand_draw at :171 and _draw at :183). The sim's post-draw slot, on_player_turn_started (player.py:186), is available and unused -- the same one-line fix as the other misplaced-slot units, and the population is reproducible with `py audit/tools/power_census.py slots`. DORMANT on its own: the decay is pure bookkeeping and nothing between the two points reads Plating's Amount (the block was already gained last turn end). Named trigger: any draw-time or BeforeHandDraw effect that reads the stack count -- power/hello_world shares this pre-draw slot. The ENEMY leg is turn_structure's G5 again.

guards.rationale: powers.py:1058-1061 passes props=ValueProp.UNPOWERED explicitly. Correct, and worth recording: this is the exact call shape whose OMITTED props made power/feel_no_pain and power/curl_up live gaps (the main report's section 4 item 4 names Plating as one of the eight siblings that get it right), and BlockCmd.apply's gate (cmds.py:145) then skips both the additive and the multiplicative block families -- so Plating's block ignores Dexterity/Frail AND ignores power/no_block and power/unmovable, matching C#, whose NoBlockPower.cs:36-39 and UnmovablePower.cs:27-30 both bail on Unpowered / non-card-or-move props.
powers.py:1069 / :1077 self-filter on the owner instead. Equivalent for the player side; for the enemy side it is the same per-creature-vs-per-side question turn_structure G5 owns.

guards.what: PlatingPower.cs:72 the turn-1 / round-1 decay exclusion
guards.rationale: C# skips the decay when the owner is a player on PlayerCombatState.TurnNumber == 1 or an enemy on combatState.RoundNumber == 1 -- so the stack the player just applied is not immediately eaten. powers.py:1063-1066 uses one test, combat.turn > 1, for both legs. Equivalent for the ported content: the sim's combat.turn is the round counter and starts at 1, and the player and the enemies share it.

guards.what: PlatingPower.cs:76 vs :80 -- ModifyAmount(-Decrement) for enemies, plain Decrement for players
guards.rationale: Two code paths that differ only by the multiplayer Decrement var, which is 1 at one player (PlatingPower.cs:27's CanonicalVars default, and :33 only raises it for enemies by Players.Count == 1). The sim's single _tick (powers.py:1066) is both. See also The sim's Power._tick (powers.py:70-75) decrements the field and _expires at <= 0 where C# routes through PowerCmd.Decrement -> ModifyAmount -> ShouldRemoveDueToAmount (PowerCmd.cs:215-250); PowerCmd.Decrement, NOT TickDownDuration, so neither side honours SkipNextDurationTick. Observationally identical -- ModifyAmount's only unconditional modifier leg is Hook.ModifyPowerAmountReceived (PowerCmd.cs:234), whose ported listeners are ArtifactPower (Debuff-only) and RuinedHelmet (StrengthPower-only). Same mechanism and same verdict as audit/records/power/colossus.json's AfterSideTurnEnd guard, per binding rule 3.

guards.what: The sim ADDS `not self.owner.is_dead` to the enemy block gain
guards.rationale: powers.py:1077. C# has no such test, but a dead creature has already had its powers stripped by Creature.RemoveAllPowersAfterDeath (Creature.cs:668-671), so the hook is unreachable on a dead owner in the game too. Defensive, not divergent. Note the PLAYER leg (:1069) does NOT carry the same guard, which is an internal inconsistency rather than a divergence.
